From 52025ebaa29f4eb4ed8bf92ce83a68f24ab7fdf7 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Weiming Shi <bestswngs@gmail.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 14:10:58 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] netfilter: nfnetlink_log: fix uninitialized padding leak in
 NFULA_PAYLOAD

__build_packet_message() manually constructs the NFULA_PAYLOAD netlink
attribute using skb_put() and skb_copy_bits(), bypassing the standard
nla_reserve()/nla_put() helpers. While nla_total_size(data_len) bytes
are allocated (including NLA alignment padding), only data_len bytes
of actual packet data are copied. The trailing nla_padlen(data_len)
bytes (1-3 when data_len is not 4-byte aligned) are never initialized,
leaking stale heap contents to userspace via the NFLOG netlink socket.

Replace the manual attribute construction with nla_reserve(), which
handles the tailroom check, header setup, and padding zeroing via
__nla_reserve(). The subsequent skb_copy_bits() fills in the payload
data on top of the properly initialized attribute.

Fixes: df6fb868d611 ("[NETFILTER]: nfnetlink: convert to generic netlink attribute functions")
Reported-by: Xiang Mei <xmei5@asu.edu>
Signed-off-by: Weiming Shi <bestswngs@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Florian Westphal <fw@strlen.de>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>

diff --git a/net/netfilter/nfnetlink_log.c b/net/netfilter/nfnetlink_log.c
index b35a90955e2e..fcbe54940b2e 100644
--- a/net/netfilter/nfnetlink_log.c
+++ b/net/netfilter/nfnetlink_log.c
@@ -647,15 +647,11 @@ __build_packet_message(struct nfnl_log_net *log,
 
 	if (data_len) {
 		struct nlattr *nla;
-		int size = nla_attr_size(data_len);
 
-		if (skb_tailroom(inst->skb) < nla_total_size(data_len))
+		nla = nla_reserve(inst->skb, NFULA_PAYLOAD, data_len);
+		if (!nla)
 			goto nla_put_failure;
 
-		nla = skb_put(inst->skb, nla_total_size(data_len));
-		nla->nla_type = NFULA_PAYLOAD;
-		nla->nla_len = size;
-
 		if (skb_copy_bits(skb, 0, nla_data(nla), data_len))
 			BUG();
 	}
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### File Modified: `net/netfilter/nfnetlink_log.c`

- **Location:** In the `__build_packet_message()` function, specifically the section that constructs the `NFULA_PAYLOAD` netlink attribute when `data_len > 0`.

- **Before the patch:**  
  The attribute was built manually using `skb_put()` to allocate space, then setting `nla_type` and `nla_len` fields directly, and finally copying payload data with `skb_copy_bits()`. This approach left the trailing alignment padding (1–3 bytes when `data_len` is not 4-byte aligned) uninitialized, leaking stale heap memory to userspace.

- **After the patch:**  
  The manual construction is replaced with a call to `nla_reserve()`. This helper automatically checks tailroom, reserves enough space for the attribute (including header and padding), sets `nla_type` and `nla_len`, and **zeroes out** any padding bytes. The subsequent `skb_copy_bits()` copies the actual payload data on top of the properly initialized attribute, eliminating the information leak.

- **Error handling change:**  
  Instead of checking tailroom manually, the code now checks the return value of `nla_reserve()` (`NULL` indicates failure) and jumps to the `nla_put_failure` label.

### Relationship

The modifications in this single file directly fix a security issue (uninitialized padding leak) by switching from a manual attribute-building pattern to the standard netlink attribute helper (`nla_reserve`), which guarantees that padding bytes are zeroed. This ensures that no stale kernel heap data is exposed to userspace via the NFLOG netlink socket.
